A.explanation: The readings 80.2, 80.1, 80.2 kg agree within $0.1\text{ kg}$, so precision is good, and they are about $5\text{ kg}$ from $75.2\text{ kg}$, so accuracy is poor.

B.explanation: The spread is only $80.2-80.1 = 0.1\text{ kg}$, so the scales do repeat to within $\pm 0.1\text{ kg}$ even though they are far from the true value.

C.explanation: Repeatability is good but closeness to the true $75.2\text{ kg}$ is not, since $80.1-75.2 \approx 4.9\text{ kg}$ which is much larger than $0.1\text{ kg}$.

D.explanation: Readings agree to $\pm 0.1\text{ kg}$ showing high precision, but all are about $5.0\text{ kg}$ high showing low accuracy due to systematic error.

Check if the $0.1\text{ kg}$ spread among readings fits within $\pm 0.1\text{ kg}$, and check if the roughly $80.2-75.2 = 5.0\text{ kg}$ shift fits within $\pm 0.1\text{ kg}$.
walkthrough: Identify the data: true mass $= 75.2\text{ kg}$, readings $= 80.2\text{ kg}$, $80.1\text{ kg}$, $80.2\text{ kg}$.
State the rules: precision is shown by small spread on repetition, accuracy is shown by small difference from the true value.
Test precision: maximum difference $= 80.2 - 80.1 = 0.1\text{ kg}$, so repeated values agree to about $\pm 0.1\text{ kg}$.
Test accuracy: typical error $\approx 80.2 - 75.2 = 5.0\text{ kg}$, which is much larger than $0.1\text{ kg}$, so there is a large systematic shift.
